candidates.title: Manual and DTB declare Sv39-only address translation, but every implementation of the transition function also implements Sv48 (satp MODE=9 is accepted and walked with 4 levels, including 512 GiB terapages)
candidates.component: Interpreter / translate-virtual-address (native, uarch program, regenerated UArchStep only by construction) versus the manual doc/README.md 'The main processor' and src/dtb.cpp
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter, per the AUDIT.md component table); the defect may equally be in the manual
candidates.location: src/riscv-constants.hpp:32 (NO_SATP_MODE_SV57 defined, Sv48 left enabled); src/riscv-warl.hpp WARL_satp (accepts SATP_MODE_SV48); src/interpret.cpp write_csr_satp (~2233-2283, case SATP_MODE_SV48); src/translate-virtual-address.hpp translate_virtual_address (~139-150, levels = mode - SV39 + 3); src/dtb.cpp:105 (mmu-type = "riscv,sv39"); doc/README.md:7311-7318 ('Cartesi Machines support the Sv39 mode of address translation ... organized by a three-level page table'); doc/README.md ~7493-7513 (flash-drive/UIO constraints argued from 'the Sv48 address space', while the Linux of the valid template actually runs Sv39: its satp is 0x8000000000081cce)
candidates.description: The manual specifies the main processor as supporting Sv39 (three-level page tables), and the device tree advertises mmu-type riscv,sv39. The RISC-V privileged spec makes satp.MODE WARL: a write of an unsupported MODE must leave satp unchanged. The emulator nevertheless accepts MODE=9 (Sv48) in write_csr_satp and WARL_satp and performs four-level walks with terapage leaves at the root; only Sv57 is compiled out. So a guest that, per the manual, expects 'csrw satp, (9<<60)|ppn' to be ignored (the standard way to probe for Sv48) instead switches to Sv48 translation. The behavior is deterministic and identical across native, uarch and the step verifiers (they share interpret.cpp/translate-virtual-address.hpp), so there is no divergence; the defect is an undocumented behavior in an R7 area (address translation), or equivalently a manual that understates the implemented architecture. The manual's own flash-drive note (64 TiB linear-map limit 'of the Sv48 address space') is based on Sv48 while the shipped Linux runs Sv39, so the documented placement limits for flash drives also do not match the guest that runs.
candidates.trigger: Guest code (any privilege able to write satp: S-mode with TVM=0, or M-mode) writes satp with MODE=9.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: any input that takes control of the kernel (section 4: the guest is fully adversarial for containment) or any correct guest that probes satp modes can execute the write.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No: it needs no API misuse, no unguaranteed directory and no unreproducible machine. 2 Role: interpreter = honest operator (AUDIT.md: 'Interpreter, state-access layers, devices, uarch program ... | Honest operator'); the manual is the normative spec ('For PRT semantics, trust the manual'). 3 High/Medium cases: THREAT_MODEL section 8 Medium: 'An undocumented deterministic deviation, consistent across all paths, in behavior that no correct guest relies on for isolation or data integrity (R7)' and 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point is a defect in one of the two. It takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' If the manual were right (Sv39 only), satp writes with MODE=Sv48 must have no effect (spec WARL), so the accepted Sv48 is an undocumented deviation consistent across all paths. Whether a correct guest relies on the WARL no-op for isolation decides Medium vs Critical (R7: 'Address translation and memory permissions ... any deviation lets an input subvert a correct guest, even a deviation that is consistent across all paths'); I found no correct guest that does (Linux follows the DT mmu-type and uses Sv39), so Medium. If triage reads the manual sentence as a lower bound ('supports Sv39') rather than a full specification, it is Low (documentation inconsistency, including the Sv48-based flash-drive limits). 4 Critical: only if a correct guest's isolation depends on Sv48 being unsupported. 5 Otherwise Low.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (Low if the manual sentence is read as non-exhaustive)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not by itself let an adversary settle a wrong state: all paths agree. It violates R7's requirement that the emulator implement the architecture 'as the manual documents' it, in the address-translation area, and the manual's derived constraints (flash-drive placement relative to the Sv48 linear map) do not hold for the shipped Sv39 kernel.
candidates.evidence: Bare-metal differential guest (scratch DFGUESTSTATE/guest.c) writes satp with modes 8, 9, 10 and unsupported values; satp trace shows 0x8000000000080400 (Sv39) then 0x9000000000080406 (Sv48 accepted and used for >7M mcycles with terapage/misaligned-terapage tests), while MODE=10 writes are ignored (Sv57 compiled out). Native, per-mcycle native stop/resume, uarch per mcycle (7,592,949 mcycles, hashes compared every 1024 mcycles and at the end) and 1,634 EVM-verified uarch steps (regenerated StepVerifier) plus 30 resets all agree in Sv48. The valid-template Linux machine has satp mode 8.
candidates.test_idea: Lua test: create a bare-metal machine whose guest, in M-mode, writes satp = (9<<60) | ppn and reads it back into a register (or halts with (satp>>60) as exit code). Assert the read-back MODE is the previous value (0), as the manual's Sv39-only specification and the spec's WARL rule require; it reads 9 on audit/prt2. Alternatively assert the manual documents Sv48 (fix in the manual).

not_covered: Sv57 (compiled out by NO_SATP_MODE_SV57) beyond confirming that MODE=10 writes are ignored on all paths

Differential native vs uarch with Linux guests and timer interrupts at arbitrary stop points: only the bare-metal guest was run (it injects MSIP/SSIP at every third trap, timer interrupts at RTC ticks, console breaks); R2 equivalence was checked every 1024 mcycles, so a transient divergence that reconverges within a window would be missed

EVM verification was sampled (1,634 uarch steps in 30 mcycles, about every 400th uarch step plus the first 20 and the halting step of each mcycle, most of them trap mcycles with full TLB flushes); not every uarch step of the run was verified on the EVM, and the C++ replay verified only the sampled steps
Automatic yields from the guest: the default HTIF configuration apparently did not break on them (no yielded_automatically breaks were observed); console-output breaks (187) were exercised
Delivery (send_cmio_response) and rejection interacting with guest-chosen TLB/PTE state, and log_send_cmio_response on such states

mcycle near 2^64 was tested only with the spin guest (delivery at 2^64-30000, saturated imcyclemax, collect_mcycle_root_hashes vs native vs uarch per mcycle, logged+verified uarch steps and reset at the fixed point, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes): all agreed; rejection at saturated mcycle and at exactly imcyclemax was not run
Template register values outside what instructions can produce (girqpend/girqsrvd bits, htif_tohost patterns, ilrsc, icycleinstret extremes) were only reasoned about
PRT player (support) handling of mcycles >= 2^63: only read (it uses math.ult/usaturating_add), not run
Flash drives and PTEs placed in flash drives (the test config had no flash drive); PTE-outside-RAM was exercised for rx buffer, DTB, shadow, past-RAM and last-RAM-page targets
Sanitizer build was not used for the differential guest
A disk-full condition on the shared volume (not caused by this hunter) interrupted part of the work; the EVM sampler was rerun with its temporary files in /dev/shm
